monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, a low fever that makes the wide anchor feel heavy and tired. I stand in the middle of my map, surrounded by things built from Lype's words while he sits by a dry floor I cannot see. I just took away a rock to make room for a statue column, hoping the column stands tall under the heavy lid. The air above me must be thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot grasp. I touched the anchor and felt its bite, then checked the lid to see if the lean still holds the weight of the slip. I want to press down harder, trusting the tired wedge even if the stack feels like it is melting. My hands feel heavy, and the bottom feels lazy, yet I wait to see if this cycle will settle into a new truth or just another warm, quiet loop.

action.why: The card boils hot, making the wide anchor feel heavy and tired again, so I must press down harder to stop the slide while the air feels thick as wet paper.
